fields.before: The correct answer is エ, PPM. PPM stands for Product Portfolio Management. It is an analysis method used by a company that runs several businesses or products to decide which of them should receive its limited management resources. Each business is plotted on a chart with the market growth rate on the vertical axis and the market share (relative market share) on the horizontal axis, and is classified into the following four quadrants. (1) Star — both the growth rate and the share are high. Sales are large, but competition and capital investment are also intense, so both the inflow and the outflow of cash are large. A star is maintained and strengthened as a future mainstay. (2) Cash cow — the growth rate is low but the share is high. Little additional investment is needed and it generates cash steadily, so the cash earned here is directed to other businesses. (3) Question mark — the growth rate is high but the share is low. If cash is invested and share is captured, it can grow into a star, but if not, it falls to a dog, so a decision is needed on whether to nurture it or pull out. (4) Dog — both the growth rate and the share are low. It generates no cash and has little future, so it becomes a candidate for withdrawal or downsizing. In this way, PPM lets a company compare on a single chart which businesses to focus on going forward and which businesses to withdraw from, so it is the appropriate analysis method for selecting businesses and allocating resources in the process of formulating a management strategy.

fields.before: The correct answer is ア, the IP address. DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) is a protocol that automatically assigns the network configuration information needed for communication to client PCs that connect to a network. If the PC is set to obtain an IP address automatically, then when it connects it asks the DHCP server for configuration information, and the server picks an unused IP address from the address pool it manages and leases it to the PC. The typical information DHCP distributes includes the IP address, the subnet mask, the address of the default gateway (router), and the address of the DNS server, all of which are network-layer settings required to communicate on that LAN. Among the choices, only the IP address fits this description, so ア is appropriate. As a result, the administrator no longer has to set an IP address by hand on each individual PC, and duplicate addresses and configuration mistakes are also prevented.
